messages:
maria: FYI support ticket #4521 — acme-prod reports p99 spike on text-gen endpoint, started ~2025-08-12T12:12Z. customer saw timeout + retries. @dan can you triage? :eyes:
ops-bot: alert: model=text-gen-std tenant=acme-prod metric=p99_latency value=3.9s window=5m link=https://dash/reports/4521
dan: on it. do we have recent batching config pushes for that fleet? any deploys around 12:00Z?
maria: we pushed a config tweak at 11:58Z for continuous-batcher defaults (auto-tuning experiment). snippet from rollout: ```json
{"auto_batching": true, "max_batch_size": 64, "wait_ms": 50, "backpressure_policy": "adaptive"}
```
maria: customer says majority of requests are tiny prompts (~10 tokens) so probably lots of mini-bursts.
dan: 64+50 for tiny prompts can increase tail — small bursts wait to fill large batches and then one slow request drags p99. need traffic shape and qps time series. @akshay can you pull tenant qps and size histogram for that window?
akshay: pulling now — preliminary: qps baseline 20, spike to ~320 for ~85s starting 12:11:40Z. payload size histogram skewed to 8-12 tokens (85%). link: https://dash/tenants/acme-prod/4521
linh: sounds like batching hysteresis + bursty traffic. when many tiny requests arrive together, the adaptive algorithm grew batches but KV-cache misses and kernel warmups caused per-token slowdowns. i'd try reducing max_batch_size and shortening wait_ms for tiny-traffic tenants.
dan: agree. propose quick canary change on 2 nodes in the pool: max_batch_size=32 wait_ms=20 jitter_ms=15. also enable small_prompt_optimizations if available.
maria: applying canary now to pool:us-east-2 nodes [n-42,n-43] — command: ```bash
redwoodctl batch-config set --pool us-east-2 --max-batch-size 32 --wait-ms 20 --jitter-ms 15 --target-nodes n-42,n-43
```
ops-bot: deployment started by maria at 2025-08-12T12:27:00Z (canary: n-42,n-43)
dan: add a small timeout jitter to avoid synchronized flushes — jitter_ms=15 should help. also enable per-tenant burst-limit to cap instantaneous qps.
\makshay: canary metrics: after config change, p99 on canary nodes dropped from 3.7s -> 1.05s within 30s, p95 moved from 450ms -> 180ms. production still elevated on other nodes.
linh: good signal. next step: roll to remaining nodes but keep conservative limits: max_batch_size=32 wait_ms=25 for non-canary, enable prefix cache prewarm for small prompts to reduce kernel warmups. also schedule a short maintenance window to apply tenant-level burst cap (e.g., 200 qps) for acme-prod during business hours.
dan: we should also add a quick mitigation fallback: when tenant p95>1s, route to smaller-model-variant (lower throughput but predictable latency). config pseudo: ```yaml
fallback_p95_threshold: 1000ms
fallback_variant: text-gen-lite
```
maria: rolling to prod now with those conservative values, will monitor. updating ticket #4521 and pinging customer.
akshay: prod roll done at 12:35Z. early numbers: p99 cluster-wide for text-gen-std fell to 1.2s 5m rolling. still watching for recurrence.
dan: thanks all. action items: maria — update support ticket and customer comms; linh — follow-up postmortem on auto-tuning heuristic and add a safe-default for tiny-prompt tenants; akshay — add alert for sudden tenant qps jumps and auto-limit suggestion; i'll own the rollback/playbook if needed.
maria: noted. will draft message to customer explaining root cause (burst traffic + aggressive max_batch_size) and the mitigations we applied. will post follow-up summary in #postmortems tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
